head: e912bea24543bab045a9b033f437fb8774dfc768
scope: PR173 idle placement. A foreground lane router on port 18797 ran this code against the real accounts. It used copies of the dobby and severus logins, and every start set place_again_after to 3m (lane.py, lane-config.json). The second start favored dobby by capacity, and the third favored severus. Real-account checks covered a new conversation, a resume, a restart, an idle move, and an idle return. The run built the code at e912bea, and later rebases of the branch kept the same code digest. Offline tests alone cover the idle move off an account that needs a login, or whose paid-overflow reading is enabled or stale. An unknown reading takes the same branch, but no test sets it. A lane cannot keep a login requirement through its start reads, choose the result of a settings read, or turn paid overflow on. TestStatusLeavesIdleMovesOutOfItsLines covers the status filter offline, because the lane saved status -v output, which has no problem lines. record.py built the record, and its prose was edited afterwards. Unchanged historical scenarios are references and were not rerun.

matrix.scenario: dobby token is outside the four-hour refresh lead
severus token is outside the four-hour refresh lead
Lane code and executable match the build at e912bea
The lane config sets place_again_after to 3m

detail.evidence: lane.py sets it at every start. lane-config.json is the third start's config.

matrix.scenario: new is placed and receives a routed 200
resume within place_again_after stays on the account and keeps the conversation's content
At the second start, which favors dobby, a request right after the start stays on severus, because idle time counts from the start
After more than place_again_after without a request, the conversation moves to dobby for idle and keeps its content
After the third start, which favors severus, the conversation returns to severus for idle once place_again_after has passed since that start
status -v lists both moves with reason idle
cache counts both idle moves at their cache writes, because each started within an hour of the previous request
Identity is the same at the start and the end
Evidence contains no copied access token

detail.method: The record builder scanned for the exact client token and the exact tokens in the lane's login copies, before the run deleted the copies. A later scan for the sk-ant-, JWT, and Bearer token patterns and the client token covered lane-config.json, lane.py, and record.py.

prior_acceptance.status: historical reference, not rerun at this code
